authoring_rule.computed_duration: 30-day authored work + ACTINV cooling duration; q* is calibrated on this design at 30 days of cooldown for the first fixed-history replacement
authoring_rule.fixed_duration: 60 days (authored from FARIS archived fixed-history event durations)
authoring_rule.zero_unplanned: The operating-history schema has no unplanned outage/reliability model; only planned replacements are present.

external_inputs.audit: Coordinator supplies the current read-only material/data audit compatible with physics.json.
external_inputs.cross_sections: Coordinator supplies a cross_sections.xml matching the physics data identity.

matched_case.provenance: The lifetime interval and work duration are authored verification assumptions from the archived FARIS no-port__breeder fixed blanket history. The flux limit is generated as native blanket flux rate × authored interval. This creates a controlled event interval, not a measured or qualified component lifetime.

native_path: faris reactor run --activation-spectra fispact-709 produces a revalidated run.json and transport-spectra.json from the exact case scenario and physics files.
faris history from-run writes a native TransportDrivingRates record; the runner derives an authored integrated-flux limit from its blanket rate and the specified operating interval.

faris maintenance run invokes the native fixed-duration history and ACTINV decay-heat coupled history. Same scenario, physics, transport record, horizon, service limit, and energy assumptions are used for both; only maintenance duration coupling changes.

outputs.energy: The FARIS result lifetime_net_electricity_mwh is retained as native output; shared 500 MW(e) peer normalization is separate and must not overwrite it.
outputs.fixed_and_computed: FARIS native faris-maintenance-result/v0.1 JSON and faris maintenance report.

scope: Authored cold-data, two-cycle maintenance code-verification case. FARIS runs the native history and ACTINV-coupled maintenance engines. The materials and source are cold-data numerical surrogates and not experimentally validated.
